subject: Portal evidence grace-period & deprecation plan
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <security@brightleaf.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightleaf Compliance <compliance@brightleaf.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:18 -0700
Subject: Notice: evidence TTL change & request for portal handoff plan

Marcus —

Heads up from Brightleaf compliance: we are moving forward with a shorter evidence retention window for vendor portals as part of a records-minimization effort. Effective Oct 15 we will start enforcing a 365-day TTL for transient artifacts (temp credentials, signed proofs, ephemeral upload tokens) and a 3-year TTL for persistent artifacts.

We need two things from Redwood by Sep 10: a) confirmation of which Whistic/Vendr/OneTrust attachments you consider persistent vs. transient for our mapping; and b) a proposed grace-period/deprecation plan for any artifacts you currently store longer than 365 days (if applicable).

If you have a standard migration or archival pattern we can reference (or a preferred S3 presign policy to preserve hashes), please attach it. We may require a short working session with your portal steward to align on presign windows and proof rotation.

Thanks — happy to be pragmatic about exceptions if there is an operational reason.

Samantha Lee
Security Operations
Brightleaf, Inc.

Attachments: ttl-change-notice.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <security@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:02:54 -0400
Subject: Re: Notice: evidence TTL change & request for portal handoff plan

Samantha —

Appreciate the heads up. We can supply the mapping and a deprecation plan by Sep 9. High-level answers up front:

- Persistent artifacts: signed SOC 2 reports, vendor-supplied CAIQ/SIG PDFs, and artifact manifests we mark as custody records. Those are typically the 3-year class.
- Transient artifacts: pre-signed upload tokens, ephemeral proof objects (temp credentials, one-time attestation uploads), and interim QNA fragments — we treat these as 365-day or less.

Operationally, Redwood has two patterns we recommend for customers: an archival snapshot (S3 immutable export plus SHA256 manifest) for anything moving off the portal; or a hash-preservation flow where we keep only the manifest and pointer in the portal and push the binary to the customer's S3. Either approach supports TTL enforcement without losing traceability.

I'll coordinate a short ops session. Karthik, can you outline the presign/archival steps and any impact to our portal-presign TTL logic? Naomi — can you confirm whether we have any current exceptions for Brightleaf artifacts?

Thanks,
Marcus
VP, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-mapping-chart.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <security@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:15:22 -0400
Subject: Re: Notice: evidence TTL change & request for portal handoff plan

Thanks Marcus — quick ops note from the portal side:

1) Presign/TTL mechanics: our current presign tokens default to a 30-day upload window; we retain the uploaded object in the portal storage bucket and track metadata (uploader, uploaded_at, sha256, field_id). TTL enforcement is implemented as a lifecycle job that flags objects for deletion and optionally emits a hash manifest to a customer-owned S3 before deletion.

2) Grace-period workflow proposal (we propose these steps):
   - Phase 0 (now—Oct 1): run an inventory of objects older than 365 days and emit a pre-deprecation manifest to Brightleaf for review.
   - Phase 1 (Oct 15—Nov 15): mark targeted transient objects as "scheduled for archival"; generate archival snapshots (if requested) and give a 30-day retrieval window for owners to request reclassification.
   - Phase 2 (Nov 16—Dec 1): final deletion pass for non-exempt objects. Persistent artifacts remain untouched until they're in the 3-year window.

3) Exceptions: we can support documented exceptions (legal hold, open audit) submitted via our compliance intake form (link below). Exceptions will be logged and reviewed weekly.

Action items:
- Marcus: send the initial mapping and the list of field_ids we consider persistent vs transient by EOD Sep 9.
- Brightleaf: confirm whether you want archival snapshots pushed to a Brightleaf S3 bucket or delivered as a zipped manifest via DocuSign/secure link.
- Ops session: propose Tue Sep 8 10:00—11:00 PT for a 45-minute run-through.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
Portal Integrations

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bEvidenceMap, JIRA SUP-4321

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <security@brightleaf.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 15:04:07 -0400
Subject: Re: Notice: evidence TTL change & request for portal handoff plan

Samantha —

Confirming Redwood will follow the proposed Phase 0/1/2 timeline. Brightleaf option B (archive snapshots to a customer S3) is preferred by our compliance team because it keeps a canonical backup under your control. We'll prepare the manifest and the list of field_ids by EOD Sep 9 and make sure the 45-minute ops session is scheduled for Sep 8 as suggested.

If Brightleaf can send the S3 bucket ARN and the cross-account role details in advance we can pre-stage the snapshot job. If you prefer DocuSign delivery, we can also wrap the manifest and provide a signed delivery acknowledgement.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
